item.title: Four Princes, One Borrowed Crown
item.hook: You impersonate a missing princess for seven days and discover that four men—a loyal knight, a rival prince, a charming spy, and your childhood protector—know the truth. Each offers an alliance, a kiss, and a different future.

You walk back to the palace in the blue hour before dawn. Fenwick walks beside you, his hand still holding yours, and the silence between you is comfortable in a way that feels like coming home.

I am not here because of duty or obligation or a childhood promise. I am here because of you. Because you are brave and stubborn and you draw maps of places that do not exist yet." He lifts your hand to his lips and presses a kiss to your knuckles. "Because you are the only person who ever made me believe the world could be better than it is."

Your throat tightens. "Fenwick—"

"I know," he says, releasing your hand. "I know there are others. I know Aldric looks at you like you are the only light in his darkness. I know Cassian makes you laugh in ways I cannot." His smile is sad but unbroken. "But I needed you to hear it once. From me. Before the world decides what we are allowed to be."

He steps back. The gate opens. Dawn bleeds gold across the sky.

meta.title: Four Princes, One Borrowed Crown
meta.logline: You impersonate a missing princess for seven days and discover that four men—a loyal knight, a rival prince, a charming spy, and your childhood protector—know the truth. Each offers an alliance, a kiss, and a different future.

nodes.title: The Borrowed Face
nodes.body:
The mirror in the abandoned chapel shows you a stranger wearing your face.

You press your fingers to the glass, tracing the curve of a jaw that belongs to Princess Elara of Thornwall—your half-sister, the woman who vanished three nights ago and left a kingdom teetering on the edge of succession war. You look enough alike to fool a court. Barely. If you keep your voice low, your chin tilted, your eyes downcast the way Elara always held hers in portraits.

Seven days. That is what the Regent's herald proclaimed at dawn: seven days until the Crown Conclave, when Elara must appear or forfeit her throne to the next claimant. Seven days for you to walk into the lion's den wearing your sister's stolen face and buy her time to return.

You are Maren. A cartographer's daughter. A nobody with Elara's bone structure and a desperate reason to help—because if Elara loses the throne, the border treaties collapse, and your village burns first.

The chapel door groans open. Cold air rushes in, carrying the scent of pine and iron.

A man steps through the threshold. Tall, broad-shouldered, his armor dented and travel-worn. A sword hangs at his hip, its pommel shaped like a silver hawk. His eyes find you instantly, and something shifts in his expression—relief, then suspicion, then a careful blankness that tells you he has already decided what you are.

"Your Highness," he says, and the words land like a blade laid flat against your throat. "I am Sir Aldric Vane. I was assigned to protect Princess Elara three years ago. I have not left her side since." He pauses. His gaze drops to your hands—your rough, ink-stained hands, nothing like a princess's. "I know you are not her."

Your blood turns to ice.

"But I also know," he continues, stepping closer, "that if the Conclave proceeds without a princess, Thornwall falls to Cassian of Meridia. And I would sooner die than see that happen." He kneels, one knee pressed to the stone floor, his head bowed. "So I will call you Princess. I will guard you. And in return, you will tell me where the real Elara went."

You stare at the top of his dark head, at the scar that cuts through his left eyebrow, at the way his jaw tightens with the effort of kneeling before a fraud.

"Deal," you whisper.

He rises. His eyes are the grey of storm clouds, and they hold yours with an intensity that makes your chest ache in a way you cannot name.

"Then we ride for the capital at dawn," Aldric says. "And Maren—" He uses your real name like a secret. "—try not to fall in love with any of the men who will try to destroy you."

You almost laugh. Almost.

The road to Thornwall stretches before you like a held breath. Somewhere out there, your sister is missing. Somewhere ahead, three men wait who will see through your disguise, offer you their hands, and try to claim the future they believe you owe them.

You straighten your borrowed crown and step into the dark.

nodes.title: The Road Divides
nodes.body:
Dawn paints the sky in shades of bruised violet as you and Aldric ride through the Thornwood. He keeps his horse half a length behind yours, close enough to shield you, far enough to maintain the fiction that you are his princess and he your servant.

You have been riding for three hours when the road splits at a moss-covered waystone. The left path winds through open meadow toward the capital's main gate—visible, exposed, the route a real princess would take. The right path dips into a narrow gorge, shadowed and quick, where no one would expect royalty to travel.

Aldric reins his horse beside you. "The meadow road is safer from ambush," he says carefully. "But we will be seen. If anyone is watching for Elara's approach, they will know we are coming." His jaw works. "The gorge is faster. But I cannot guarantee what waits at the other end."

Before you can answer, a sound reaches you—hoofbeats, light and quick, approaching from behind. A rider emerges from the tree line on a dapple-grey mare, her cloak the deep blue of the Meridian court.

She is young, sharp-featured, and smiling with too many teeth.

"Princess Elara," she calls out, and the name sounds like a challenge. "Or should I say—whoever wears her face today?"

Aldric's hand moves to his sword. You touch his wrist to stop him.

The rider dismounts with fluid grace. "My name is Lira. I serve Prince Cassian of Meridia, who sends his regards and a proposal." She produces a sealed letter, the wax stamped with a silver serpent. "He knows the princess is missing. He knows someone will come to fill the gap. And he wants to meet you before the Conclave." Her eyes flick to Aldric with open amusement. "Alone."

Aldric steps forward, his voice low and dangerous. "The princess does not meet with rivals in secret."

"The princess does many things," Lira replies sweetly. "But you are not the princess, are you, Sir Aldric? You are her shield. And shields can be set aside."

The letter sits in Lira's outstretched hand like a dare.

You think of Cassian of Meridia—the rival claimant, the man whose ambition could unravel everything you are trying to protect. Meeting him means walking into a trap with your eyes open. Refusing means losing the chance to learn what he knows about Elara's disappearance.

The gorge path offers speed and secrecy. The meadow road offers safety and visibility. And Lira's letter offers something else entirely: the chance to face your enemy before he expects you.

Aldric watches you, waiting. His grey eyes hold a question he will not voice: Do you trust me enough to choose the safe path? Or are you already reaching for something more dangerous?

The morning wind stirs the trees. Somewhere far away, a bell tolls the hour. Seven days have become six and a half.

You must choose.

choices.text: Take the meadow road and accept Lira's letter—meet Cassian openly at the capital gates
choices.meaning: Choose visibility and confrontation; signals boldness and willingness to face Cassian directly

choices.text: Take the gorge path and refuse the letter—arrive at the capital unseen and on your own terms
choices.meaning: Choose stealth and independence; signals caution and self-reliance

nodes.title: The Serpent's Garden
nodes.body:
You take the letter.

Aldric's expression shutters closed, but he does not argue. He simply falls into step behind you as you follow Lira down the meadow road, the sealed envelope tucked inside your bodice like a coal against your ribs.

The capital of Thornwall rises from the mist like a dream of silver and stone. Its walls are pale as bone, its towers crowned with banners that snap in the wind—Elara's banners, still flying, still waiting for a princess who may never return.

Lira leads you not to the main gate but to a side entrance, where a garden spills over the ramparts in cascades of white wisteria. The scent is intoxicating, almost narcotic, and you understand why Cassian chose this place. Beauty is a weapon. It softens you before the blade arrives.

He is waiting beneath a pergola draped in flowering vines. Prince Cassian of Meridia is nothing like you imagined. You expected coldness, calculation, the sharp angles of ambition. Instead, he is warm-toned and laughing, with copper skin and dark eyes that crinkle at the corners when he smiles—which is often, and always at you.

"So you came," he says, rising from a stone bench with the easy grace of a man who has never been afraid. "I was not certain you would. Most people who receive my letters burn them unread." He gestures to the bench beside him. "Sit. I have had tea prepared. Chamomile and honey—Elara's favorite, though I suspect you are not Elara at all."

You do not sit. "You know I am not her."

"I know many things." He pours tea into two porcelain cups, his movements unhurried. "I know Elara left the palace voluntarily. I know she went south, toward the Ashenmere. I know she left because she was afraid—not of losing her throne, but of what she would become if she kept it." He slides a cup toward you. "And I know that you, whoever you are, love her enough to wear her face and walk into a court that wants to tear you apart. That makes you either very brave or very foolish."

"Perhaps both," you say.

His smile sharpens. "I like both." He sits back down, crossing one leg over the other with feline ease. "Here is my proposal. I will withdraw my claim to the throne. I will publicly support Elara—or you, in her place—at the Conclave. In exchange, you will grant me a seat on the ruling council and one favor, to be named later."

The offer is generous. Too generous. You can feel the hook beneath the bait.

"And if I refuse?"

Cassian's expression does not change, but something shifts behind his eyes—a flicker of genuine surprise, as if he expected you to accept without question. "Then I will press my claim at the Conclave, and the kingdom will fracture. I would prefer not to. I find destruction tedious." He leans forward, and his voice drops to something intimate, almost tender. "I would prefer to build something with you instead."

Aldric appears at the garden's edge, his hand on his sword, his gaze fixed on Cassian with undisguised hostility. "Your Highness. We should not linger."

Cassian glances at him with lazy amusement. "Ah, the faithful hound. Tell me, Sir Aldric—does she know you would die for her? Or do you simply hope she will notice eventually?"

Aldric's jaw tightens. You see the flush creep up his neck before he turns away.

You take the tea. You drink it. It is perfect—warm and sweet and tasting faintly of summer.

Cassian watches you drink with an expression you cannot read. Something like hunger. Something like hope.

"I will consider your proposal," you say.

"Of course you will." He stands, brushing invisible dust from his coat. "I will be at the Conclave. Wear something beautiful."

As you leave the garden, Aldric falls into step beside you. His voice is low, rough-edged. "He is dangerous."

"I know."

"You drank his tea."

"I know."

A long silence. Then, so quietly you almost miss it: "Be careful, Maren. Not everyone who offers you a hand wants to help you stand. Some want to pull you down."

You think of Cassian's smile, warm as sunlight on water. You think of the hook beneath the bait. You think of how easy it would be to fall.

The palace gates open before you. Six days remain.

choices.meaning: Enter the capital and prepare for the Conclave

nodes.title: The Gorge of Whispers
nodes.body:
You leave Lira standing in the road with her letter still extended, her smile faltering into something sharper.

"The gorge," you tell Aldric. "We go through the gorge."

He nods once, and something in his shoulders loosens—not quite relief, but the absence of the tension that had been building since Lira appeared. He turns his horse toward the narrow path without a word, and you follow him into the shadow of the cliffs.

The gorge is beautiful in a desolate way. The walls rise on either side like the ribs of some ancient beast, streaked with moss and veined with quartz that catches the thin light filtering from above. The air is cool and damp, carrying the mineral scent of deep stone.

You are halfway through when you hear the singing.

It comes from above—a low, wordless melody that seems to seep from the rock itself. Aldric draws his sword, positioning himself between you and the sound, but you place a hand on his arm.

"Wait."

A figure drops from the cliff face with the silent grace of a cat, landing in a crouch ten paces ahead. He straightens slowly, and you see a young man with pale hair the color of winter wheat and eyes so green they seem to glow in the dim light. He is lean and quick-looking, dressed in the mottled grey-green of a forest scout, and he is smiling at you with an expression of such pure, uncomplicated delight that your breath catches.

"Maren," he says. Not Your Highness. Not Princess. Your name, spoken like a prayer he has been holding for years.

"Fenwick," you whisper.

He crosses the distance between you in three strides and takes your hands in his, his fingers calloused and warm. "I knew it was you. I knew the moment I heard Elara had vanished. I knew you would come." His thumbs trace circles over your knuckles, and his eyes search your face with an intensity that makes your chest ache. "You look like her. But you move like yourself. You always did."

Aldric's voice cuts through the moment like a blade. "You know her."

Fenwick releases your hands but does not step back. "I have known her since we were children. I was her guardian before you, Sir Aldric. Before the court took her and made her into something she was not." His gaze flicks to you, softening. "I was supposed to protect her. I failed. But I will not fail you, Maren."

The words land differently than you expect. Not as a knight's oath, formal and distant, but as a promise made between equals. Fenwick does not kneel. He does not bow. He simply stands before you and offers you the truth of his presence.

"How did you find us?" Aldric asks, his hand still on his sword.

"I have been watching the gorge for three days." Fenwick's smile turns wry. "I knew someone would come this way. The meadow road is too obvious for anyone with sense." He looks at you again, and his expression is open, unguarded, almost painfully sincere. "I have information about Elara. Where she went. Why she left. But I will share it only with Maren. Alone."

Aldric's jaw tightens. "I am her guard. I go where she goes."

"You are her guard," Fenwick agrees pleasantly. "But she is not your princess. And you know it." He turns back to you, and his voice gentles. "I will not keep you long. But there are things you need to know before you walk into that palace. Things that will change what you believe about Elara, about the throne, about why she really left."

The gorge narrows around you. Above, the sky is a thin ribbon of grey. You can feel Aldric's tension like a wire drawn taut, can feel Fenwick's patience like an open hand.

You choose to listen. Fenwick leads you deeper into the gorge, to a hollow where a small fire burns and a bedroll is spread over flat stone. He sits cross-legged and gestures for you to join him.

"Elara left because she discovered something," he says, his voice low. "A document. A treaty your father signed before he died—one that would have given Meridia control of the northern passes. She went to find the original, to prove it was forged. If she succeeds, Cassian's claim collapses entirely. If she fails—" He pauses. "If she fails, the Conclave will crown him, and Thornwall will become a vassal state within a generation."

The weight of it settles over you like snowfall. Your sister did not flee from fear. She fled toward truth.

"Then we help her finish what she started," you say.

Fenwick's smile is slow, warm, and full of a hope so fragile it might shatter. "Together," he says. "Like when we were young. Like we promised."

Aldric stands at the hollow's edge, listening. His expression is unreadable, but his hand has left his sword. Something has shifted in him—a crack in the armor, a question he is not yet ready to ask.

The palace waits beyond the gorge. Five days remain.

choices.text: Continue to the palace with Fenwick's knowledge
choices.meaning: Enter the capital armed with the truth about Elara's mission

nodes.title: The Court of Masks
nodes.body:
The palace of Thornwall is a labyrinth of mirrors.

Every corridor reflects you back to yourself—Elara's face, Elara's posture, Elara's careful, measured grace. You have been here two days now, and the disguise holds, but barely. The courtiers watch you with eyes like polished stones, and you feel their suspicion like needles against your skin.

Aldric has not left your side. He sleeps outside your chamber door, eats only what he has tasted first, and positions himself between you and every shadow. It is exhausting and tender and more than you deserve.

Fenwick has vanished into the palace's hidden passages—he knows them all, he told you, from his years as Elara's childhood protector. He appears and disappears like smoke, bringing you scraps of information: which lords support Cassian, which are wavering, which can be turned.

And Cassian himself has been present at every court function, watching you from across the room with that warm, knowing smile. He has sent you three gifts—a book of poetry, a silver hairpin, a single white rose—and each one arrived with a note that made your pulse quicken in a way you refuse to examine.

Tonight is the Eve of Conclave. Tomorrow, the assembly will decide the fate of the kingdom. You stand in your chamber, staring at your reflection, when a knock comes at the door.

It is not Aldric. It is not Fenwick. It is a servant you do not recognize, carrying a tray with a single goblet of wine and a folded note.

The note reads: The Council Chamber. Midnight. Come alone, and I will show you what Elara found. —C.

Your heart hammers. Cassian knows something about Elara's mission. If he has the forged treaty—or proof of it—everything changes.

But there is another option. Fenwick sent word an hour ago that he has located a witness who can testify about the forgery. The witness is hiding in the lower city, and Fenwick needs your authority to bring them into the palace safely. It means leaving the palace tonight, slipping through the servants' gate, and trusting Fenwick completely.

Aldric appears at your shoulder, having read the note over your reflection in the mirror. His expression is grim. "It is a trap."

"Probably," you admit.

"Then do not go."

"And if he has what we need? If he can end this without bloodshed?"

Aldric is quiet for a long moment. Then: "If you go to him, I cannot follow. He will not allow it. You will be alone with a man who wants your throne." His voice drops. "I do not trust him, Maren. I do not trust the way he looks at you."

The words hang in the air between you, heavy with something neither of you has named.

Fenwick's message burns in your other hand. The witness. The lower city. The chance to build a case so airtight that no council can deny it.

Midnight approaches. The candles gutter in their sconces, casting your shadow long and wavering against the wall.

You must choose.

choices.text: Go to Cassian in the Council Chamber—risk the trap for the chance at the treaty
choices.meaning: Choose Cassian's path; signals trust in his offer and willingness to face danger for knowledge

choices.text: Go with Fenwick to the lower city—secure the witness and build an unshakeable case
choices.meaning: Choose Fenwick's path; signals trust in his plan and commitment to justice over shortcuts

nodes.title: The Serpent's Confession
nodes.body:
The Council Chamber is empty except for candlelight and Cassian.

He sits at the head of the long table, his posture deceptively relaxed, a bottle of wine and two glasses before him. When you enter, he rises—not with the performative grace of the court, but with something genuine, almost vulnerable.

"You came," he says softly. "I was not sure you would."

"You said you had something to show me."

He nods and produces a leather folio from beneath the table. Inside, you see the edge of a document—old parchment, heavy seal, the unmistakable hand of a royal scribe.

"The treaty," you breathe.

"A copy," Cassian corrects. "The original is still missing. Elara has it—or she is close to finding it. But this copy is enough to prove the forgery existed. Enough to delay the Conclave, perhaps. Enough to buy time." He slides the folio across the table. "It is yours. Freely given. No conditions."

You stare at him. "Why?"

Cassian pours wine into both glasses, his movements slow, deliberate. "Because I have spent my life building toward this moment—the moment I could claim Thornwall's throne. And then you walked into my garden, wearing a dead woman's face, and I realized I did not want the throne anymore." He meets your eyes. "I want to know what it would be like to build something instead of taking it."

The honesty of it strikes you like a physical blow. You have spent days bracing for manipulation, for hidden hooks and barbed bargains. This—this raw, unguarded admission—is more dangerous than any trap.

"You are lying," you say, but your voice wavers.

"Am I?" He moves closer, and the candlelight catches the gold in his dark eyes. "I have lied to every person in this court. I have smiled at men I despised and flattered women I pitied. But I have not lied to you, Maren. Not once. Not since the garden." His hand rises, hovering near your face without touching. "May I?"

You nod. You do not know why you nod.

His fingers brush your cheek—light as a whisper, warm as a promise. His touch traces the line of your jaw, and you feel the disguise dissolve beneath his hand, feel yourself become not Elara, not the princess, but simply yourself.

"There," he murmurs. "That is the face I wanted to see."

He kisses you. It is gentle, questioning, a kiss that asks permission with every breath. His hand cups your jaw, his thumb stroking your cheekbone, and when you kiss him back, he makes a sound low in his throat—surprise, relief, something like gratitude.

When you pull apart, his forehead rests against yours. "Stay," he whispers. "Not as Elara. As yourself. Stay, and we will find another way."

The door opens.

Aldric stands in the threshold, his face a mask of controlled fury. His eyes move from Cassian's hand on your face to the folio on the table to your flushed cheeks, and something breaks behind his expression—a wall crumbling, a hope dying.

"Your Highness," he says, and the title is a blade. "The Conclave begins at dawn. You should rest."

He turns and leaves. The sound of his footsteps fading down the corridor is the loneliest sound you have ever heard.

Cassian watches him go, then looks back at you with an expression that is equal parts triumph and guilt. "He loves you," he says quietly. "You know that."

"I know."

"And you love him back."

You do not answer. You take the folio and walk toward the door. Behind you, Cassian says nothing. He does not need to. The silence says everything.

Dawn is coming. The Conclave awaits. And three men stand between you and the future you choose.

nodes.title: The Witness Below
nodes.body:
The lower city smells of woodsmoke and river mud.

Fenwick moves through the streets like water through stone—fluid, silent, certain. He keeps close to you, his shoulder brushing yours with every turn, and you realize he is not just guiding you. He is shielding you. His body is a wall between you and the dark.

"The witness is a scribe," he explains in a low voice as you duck beneath a low archway. "She worked in the royal scriptorium when the treaty was forged. She saw the original destroyed and the copy made. She has been hiding for three years, terrified that whoever ordered the forgery would find her."

"And you convinced her to testify?"

Fenwick's smile is rueful. "I convinced her that you are not Elara. That you are Maren—the girl who used to sneak into the palace gardens and draw maps in the dirt." He glances at you, and his eyes are warm with memory. "She remembers you. She said you were the only person in the palace who ever asked her name."

The memory surfaces like a bubble from deep water. You were twelve, sketching the garden paths in charcoal, and a young woman had stopped to watch. You had asked her name. She had looked startled, as if no one had asked in a long time.

"Her name is Doss," you say.

"Her name is Doss," Fenwick confirms. "And she is waiting for us in a tavern called the Broken Compass."

The tavern is warm and dim, its air thick with the smell of ale and roasting meat. In the back corner, a woman sits hunched over a cup, her face half-hidden by a hood. When she sees you, her eyes widen.

"You came," she whispers. "You actually came."

"I promised," you say, though you do not remember promising. But Maren-the-child would have. Maren-the-child promised things easily, before the world taught her how expensive promises could be.

Doss talks for an hour. She tells you about the night the treaty was forged—how she was called to the scriptorium after midnight, how she saw the royal seal pressed into wax by hands that were not the king's, how the original was fed to a fire while she watched from behind a pillar, trembling.

"It was Lord Vane," she says finally. "Aldric's father. He forged the treaty on Cassian's orders. That is why Aldric guards the princess so fiercely. He is trying to atone for his father's sin."

The revelation hits you like cold water. Aldric's devotion, his intensity, his desperate need to protect Elara—it is not just duty. It is penance.

Fenwick's hand finds yours beneath the table. His fingers interlace with yours, warm and steady. "We have what we need," he says softly. "Tomorrow, we present this to the Conclave, and the truth wins."

You walk back to the palace in the blue hour before dawn. Fenwick walks beside you, his hand still holding yours, and the silence between you is comfortable in a way that feels like coming home.

At the servants' gate, he stops. "Maren." His voice is careful, measured, as if he is handling something fragile. "Whatever happens tomorrow—I need you to know that I am not here because of Elara. I am not here because of duty or obligation or a childhood promise. I am here because of you. Because you are brave and stubborn and you draw maps of places that do not exist yet." He lifts your hand to his lips and presses a kiss to your knuckles. "Because you are the only person who ever made me believe the world could be better than it is."

Your throat tightens. "Fenwick—"

"I know," he says, releasing your hand. "I know there are others. I know Aldric looks at you like you are the only light in his darkness. I know Cassian makes you laugh in ways I cannot." His smile is sad but unbroken. "But I needed you to hear it once. From me. Before the world decides what we are allowed to be."

He steps back. The gate opens. Dawn bleeds gold across the sky.

The Conclave awaits.

nodes.title: The Conclave of Crowns
nodes.body:
The Great Hall of Thornwall is a cathedral of light and ambition.

A hundred lords and ladies fill the tiered galleries, their silks and jewels catching the morning sun that pours through the stained-glass windows. The air hums with whispered alliances and barely concealed hostilities. At the center of it all stands the Throne of Ash—a seat carved from the heartwood of the first tree ever planted in Thornwall, its arms worn smooth by generations of royal hands.

You stand before it wearing Elara's face and your own courage.

The evidence is ready. Whether it is the treaty copy or Doss's testimony, you have enough to challenge Cassian's claim. But the Conclave is not only about evidence. It is about who stands beside you. Who the court sees at your right hand. Who you trust with the future.

Three men stand in the hall, each watching you from a different point in the crowd.

Aldric is at the base of the throne, his hand on his sword, his grey eyes fixed on you with an intensity that burns. He has not spoken to you since the Council Chamber—since he saw Cassian's hand on your face. But he is here. He will always be here. That is both his devotion and his wound.

Cassian stands among the Meridian delegation, resplendent in midnight blue, his expression unreadable. When your eyes meet, he inclines his head—a gesture that might be respect, might be challenge, might be surrender. You cannot tell. Perhaps he wants you to wonder.

Fenwick is nowhere to be seen—but you feel him. A presence at the edge of perception, a whisper in the rafters, a shadow that moves when you are not looking directly at it. He is here. He is always here. That is both his gift and his grief.

The Chancellor calls the assembly to order. "The Conclave is convened. The claimant to the Throne of Ash will present her case."

You step forward. The hall falls silent.

And then you must choose. Not just what to say, but who to say it with. Who will stand at your side when the truth is spoken. Who will hold the future you are building.

Aldric steps forward first, his voice carrying across the silence. "Your Highness. Whatever you decide—I am yours. Not the princess's. Yours." It is the first time he has said it openly. The court hears it. The court will remember.

Cassian moves next, crossing the floor with unhurried grace until he stands before you, close enough that only you can hear his words. "Choose me, and I will give you everything. Not a throne—a partnership. Not a crown—a life." His dark eyes hold yours, and for the first time, you see no calculation in them. Only want.

And then—a hand on your shoulder. Fenwick, materializing from the crowd like a dream taking shape. His green eyes are steady, his voice quiet but carrying. "You do not need a crown, Maren. You never did. You need someone who sees you. I see you. I have always seen you."

The hall waits. The throne waits. Three men wait.

You draw a breath that feels like the first breath you have taken in seven days.

You choose.

choices.text: Take Aldric's hand and name him your champion—choose the knight who loved you before he knew your name

nodes.title: The Knight's Oath
nodes.body:
You take Aldric's hand.

The hall erupts. Lords shout, ladies gasp, the Chancellor sputters—but none of it matters. What matters is the way Aldric's fingers close around yours, tight and trembling, as if he is afraid you will dissolve like morning frost.

You present the evidence. The forgery is exposed. Cassian withdraws his claim with a grace that surprises everyone—himself included, perhaps. He bows to you from across the hall, and his smile is genuine, if tinged with something bittersweet.

Later, in the quiet of the throne room, Aldric kneels before you. Not as a knight before a princess. As a man before the woman he loves.

"I was assigned to protect Elara," he says, his voice rough. "But somewhere between the chapel and the Conclave, I stopped guarding a crown and started guarding a person. Your person." He looks up, and his grey eyes are naked with feeling. "I know I am not easy. I know I am rigid and suspicious and I push everyone away. But I will not push you away. I swear it on my sword, on my name, on every oath I have ever spoken. You are mine to protect, and I am yours to keep."

You kneel before him—something no princess would do, something only Maren would do—and you take his face in your hands.

"I am not Elara," you say.

"I know."

"I am a cartographer's daughter with ink on her fingers and no claim to any throne."

"I know."

"And you love me anyway."

His answer is a kiss—fierce and tender and tasting of salt, because you are both crying, though neither of you will admit it later.

You do not take the throne. You name a regent, expose the forgery publicly, and ensure Elara's return is met with justice rather than suspicion. Then you leave the palace with Aldric at your side, his hand in yours, his armor left behind.

He builds you a house on the border of the Thornwood, where the maps you draw hang on every wall and his sword rests above the mantel—unused, unneeded, because the only thing he guards now is your heart.

And he guards it well.

nodes.title: The Serpent's Heart
nodes.body:
You take Cassian's hand.

The hall goes silent—not with shock, but with the held breath of a hundred people watching history reshape itself before their eyes.

Cassian's fingers lace through yours, warm and certain. He does not pull you toward the throne. He turns you toward the assembly and speaks, his voice carrying with the effortless authority of a man born to command.

"I withdraw my claim," he says. "Not in defeat. In partnership." He lifts your joined hands. "This woman—this extraordinary, impossible woman—has shown me that a throne is not a prize to be won. It is a responsibility to be shared. I will not rule Thornwall. But I will stand beside whoever does, as counselor, as ally, as—" He pauses, and his dark eyes find yours, and his voice softens to something only you can hear. "As hers. If she will have me."

You present the evidence together. The forgery is exposed. The council is reformed. And when it is over, when the lords have filed out and the hall is empty except for dust motes and fading light, Cassian turns to you with an expression you have never seen on his face before.

Uncertainty.

"I have spent my life performing," he says quietly. "Smiling when I wanted to snarl. Offering when I wanted to take. I do not know how to be honest." He swallows. "But I am trying to be honest now. I love you. Not the disguise. Not the princess. You. The woman who drank my tea and walked into my garden and looked at me like I was worth more than my ambition."

You step closer. "You are worth more than your ambition."

"Then stay," he whispers. "Not as a queen. Not as a pawn. As my equal. As my—" He stops. Starts again. "As the person who makes me want to be better."

You kiss him in the empty throne room, surrounded by the ghosts of kings who never thought to ask what love might look like on a throne. His arms wrap around you, pulling you close, and his forehead drops to yours with a sigh that sounds like surrender.

You rule together. Not from the Throne of Ash, but from a new council—equal voices, equal power, equal say. It is unprecedented. It is difficult. It is extraordinary.

And every evening, when the court has emptied and the candles burn low, Cassian pours you tea—chamomile and honey—and asks you about your day with the focused attention of a man who has finally found the one thing worth paying attention to.

You.

nodes.title: The Map Without Borders
nodes.body:
You take Fenwick's hand and walk away from the throne.

The hall erupts behind you—shouts, protests, the Chancellor's gavel banging uselessly—but you do not turn around. Fenwick's hand is warm in yours, his stride matching yours perfectly, as if your bodies remember how to move together from a thousand childhood games in palace gardens.

You walk through the Great Hall, down the corridor of mirrors, past the throne room and the council chambers and the rooms where power is hoarded like gold. You walk until the palace walls give way to gardens, and the gardens give way to open fields, and the fields stretch before you like a map with no borders.

Fenwick stops at the edge of the Thornwood. The morning light catches his pale hair and turns it to gold. His green eyes are bright with tears he will not shed.

"You left the throne," he says, as if he still cannot believe it.

"I left a borrowed crown," you correct. "I was never meant to wear it."

He laughs—a sound like water over smooth stones—and pulls you into his arms. His embrace is not the careful, measured touch of a courtier or the fierce grip of a knight. It is the hold of someone who has been waiting years for this moment and is terrified it will vanish if he loosens his grip.

"I drew maps," you murmur into his shoulder. "When I was young. Maps of places that did not exist yet."

"I know," he says. "I kept them. Every one. They are in my pack right now." He pulls back, smiling through his tears. "I thought maybe someday we would go find them. The places you imagined. The ones that do not exist yet."

You look at him—this man who has loved you since you were both children with dirt on your hands and stars in your eyes. This man who never asked you to be a princess, never asked you to wear a crown, never asked you to be anything other than exactly what you are.

"Together?" you ask.

"Together," he says. "Like we promised."

You leave Thornwall behind. The Conclave resolves itself without you—the forgery is exposed, Elara returns, the kingdom heals. But that is a story for other people to tell.

Your story is the open road. The blank spaces on the map. The places that do not exist yet, waiting for you to walk them into being.

Fenwick walks beside you, his hand in yours, his laughter carrying on the wind. And ahead, always ahead, the horizon stretches like a promise.

You draw new maps. And this time, the places are real.

recommendation.summary: Step into the borrowed face of a vanished princess and survive seven days of court intrigue where every smile hides a blade. Four men know your secret—a loyal knight, a rival prince, a charming spy, and your childhood protector—and each offers a different alliance, a different kiss, and a different future. Navigate branching paths through palace gardens and hidden gorges, choose between risky diplomacy and unshakeable evidence, and ultimately decide whose hand to take at the Conclave of Crowns. Will you claim the throne beside your champion, stand as an equal with a former rival, or walk away from power entirely with the one who sees only you?
